  -expires string
    	new last day the fact is worth recalling, YYYY-MM-DD; empty keeps the current one
  -force
    	store it even when it looks like a secret
  -keywords string

  -no-expires

input.command: memcue correct -keywords "larkspur,http3,http/3,quic,h3" 01M5Z7Q8J7MV3BM5H6A21WC8HS -- "Larkspur 2.0.0 added HTTP/3 support, experimental and off by default; enabled with the --h3 flag or Client{H3: true}. Larkspur 1.8 did not support HTTP/3. Source: Larkspur changelog 2.0.0 (2026-08-14) and 1.8.0 (2025-10-02)."
input.description: Update stale HTTP/3 fact on research shelf

final.result:
**Yes, since 2.0.0 (2026-08-14).** HTTP/3 support is still experimental and off by default. You turn it on with the `--h3` flag or `Client{H3: true}`. Version 1.8.0 didn't support it.

I also updated an old research note that said Larkspur has no HTTP/3 support, so it now reflects 2.0.0.
